title: Bidirectional Dijkstra: Faster Routes in Woodstock!
description: Watch Bidirectional Dijkstra explore a street-map grid from both the start and destination, shrinking the search space in real time. The visualization highlights how two coordinated shortest-path frontiers meet to find an optimal route efficiently.
ig_caption:
🗺️⚡ In Woodstock (Cape Town), we’re visualizing **Bidirectional Dijkstra**—a shortest-path algorithm that runs **two Dijkstra searches at once**: one forward from the start and one backward from the goal. 

🔁 Instead of expanding outward from only one side, both frontiers grow through weighted edges until they **meet at a common node**, drastically reducing the explored area—especially on large, realistic street graphs. 

📉 Graph theory moment: your map becomes a weighted graph (streets as edges, intersections as nodes). Because edge weights represent travel cost (distance/time), Dijkstra guarantees optimality; running it bidirectionally balances work by keeping both searches near where the solution actually lies. 

🎥 Want the next visualization for your neighborhood or city? Comment your city + the kind of roads you want (hills, grid, waterfront) and **share this reel** with a friend learning algorithms! ✅
fb_caption:
🚦 Educational demo time! In this reel, **Bidirectional Dijkstra** finds the shortest path by searching from both the start and the destination simultaneously. 

📌 Turning a real street map into a weighted graph lets the algorithm expand frontiers intelligently; when the two searches meet, you get the optimal route without exploring everything. 

💬 If you enjoyed the visualization, like, share, and drop a city name for a future pathfinding video!
yt_description:
Bidirectional Dijkstra visualization on real street maps (Cape Town – Woodstock)! ✅ Watch two synchronized Dijkstra searches expand from start + goal, meet in the middle, and produce the optimal shortest path faster than one-way search. 

Keywords: bidirectional dijkstra, shortest path, pathfinding algorithm, graph search, Dijkstra’s algorithm, coding visualization, computer science education, real map algorithms, weighted graphs, intersections and roads.
